title: Dehomag, IBM's German subsidiary, ahead in transistors

tellings.quote: German subsidiary of IBM, a company called Dehomog >> was way ahead

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Dehomag, the German branch of the American computing company IBM, was far ahead in transistors, the tiny electronic switches behind modern computers, during the 1930s and 1940s. He raises it in an episode about a claimed secret Nazi UFO programme, where it would suggest Germany had advanced electronics earlier than is usually thought.
